summary: The group splits into 15 weights runs (point or tract link graphs) and 23 regression runs that almost all use one layout: a Chicago tract map of residuals on the left and coefficient bars against true-value dots on the right. Most cards scrub a Data knob: 27 of 38 do, usually the generating process (rho, lambda, noise, contrast). The best pictures are spatial-lag, gwr-nonstationarity-test, geographically-weighted-regression and multiscale-gwr, where the map shows the operation's own output and the slider changes it legibly. The weakest are spatial-regression-diagnostics (its test bars barely render at range [0, 40]), pair-gather, neighborhood-summary (dark on dark), spatial-weights-traces (no spatial picture, a spike artifact) and the chunked-weights family, which colors links by chunk and hides what the operation does. The census is wrong for the 7 runs built through shared/table-model.ts and shared/panel.ts: they do have update(), so the card scrubs `strength` or `unitEffects` per frame, not maximumPower, instrumentOrder or estimator by rebuild. Two shared files would fix many entries at once. In shared/regression.ts, drawCoefficientPanel draws signed coefficients as bars from the bottom of [-3, 3] with no zero line, so negative estimates read as small positive bars in 12 runs. In shared/weights.ts, a per-row highlight of links (`probe`) would serve all 15 weights runs. The table-model and panel runs look alike (duplicates); a probe or period playhead is the cheapest way to tell them apart.

sharedChanges.change: drawCoefficientPanel: draw bars from zero (or add a zero reference line) and use a diverging ramp for signed estimates; label the slots (intercept, x1, x2, rho/lambda). Today a -1.5 slope reads as a short positive bar.

drawTractMap defaults to range 'auto', so residual maps renormalize on every run and hide how the noise and strength sliders change magnitude; pass a fixed symmetric range (for example [-1.5, 1.5]) for residuals.

Add a helper that, given a focus row written per frame (uint32 one-row buffer), emits the focus row's link segments, so every weights run can highlight the hovered point's or tract's neighbors without a rebuild (addLinkSegments with onlyWhere already does most of this).

Distinguish the four table-model runs: give each a model-specific secondary picture (for example the lag-ML log-likelihood over rho, the 2SLS instrument WX, the error model's filtered residuals) instead of the same residual map plus bars.

Draw the residual map of one chosen period (a draw-time offset into the period-major residual buffer) so a period playhead can show the panel's time dimension; today only period 0 is drawn and the panels look like the cross-section runs.

frameworkNeeds: setPointer support in defineOperationRun: pointer in world coordinates passed to update() or to a pointer hook, which today only hand-written demos get
pointer to nearest point / containing tract polygon lookup (CPU, from the run's inputs) returning a row index
per-frame highlight on polygons, dots and lines layers (a focus row id or a uint32 highlight buffer) without rebuild
cursor glyphs: ring of a world-space radius, crosshair, vertical boundary line, and kernel-footprint shading
chart reference marks: zero line, slot labels and a highlighted bar or x position on bars/line charts
draw-time offset or count on a value buffer so one layer can show period p of a period-major buffer
debounced snapping or a small pre-built variant cache for compile-time props (bandwidth of weights transforms, tolerance, maximumIterations)
census.mjs should resolve update() through shared run factories (defineTableModelRun, definePanelRun); it misreports 7 runs as rebuild
